tagline: Down Breakneck Hill to a colonial road and a lottery house.
intro: From the Route 146 cloverleaf, Breakneck Hill Road pitches steeply down the Moshassuck River valley, winding between rock outcrops under mixed hardwoods with Lincoln Woods State Park along its south side. At the bottom it meets Great Road and the grade eases onto the flood plain, past Butterfly Pond and open fields with a towering sycamore.

Great Road was laid out in 1683 to carry trade between Providence and Mendon, and it was not widened and paved until 1926. The stretch between the old Butterfly Mill and the Arnold House still keeps closest to its early course.

moments.title: Hearthside
moments.text: Stephen Smith is said to have built this fieldstone house of ten hearths with Louisiana lottery winnings to win a Providence woman, who turned down both him and the house.

moments.title: Chase Farm
moments.text: A large dairy farm at the turn of the last century and one of Lincoln's last working farms until 1965, it was sold to the town in 1979 as open land.

moments.title: Eleazer Arnold House
moments.text: Just past the eastern end stands a stone-ender, its exposed fieldstone end walls a style brought over from the west of England, now a National Historic Landmark owned by Historic New England.

sources.label: RIDOT, Breakneck Hill Road / Great Road Scenic Highway Stewardship Plan (2003), pages 1 to 8
